plain_english: O Lord, what is the Unsurpassable that grants Kaula fruit at once — known by a mere touch of knowing, rising to kinship with the Sky-Goer?
sanskrit_cite: anuttaraṃ kathaṃ deva sadyaḥ kaulikasiddhidam | yena vijñātamātreṇa khecarīsamatāṃ brajet

plain_english: Tell me this secret of secrets, Lord — the Power that dwells in the heart, Kaulikī, mistress of the clan.
sanskrit_cite: etadguhyaṃ mahāguhyaṃ kathayasva mama prabho | hṛdayasthā tu yā śaktiḥ kaulikī kulanāyikā

plain_english: Tell me of her, Lord of gods, by whom I come to fullness. — Hear, blessed Goddess: even the answer has one beyond it — the Unsurpassable.
sanskrit_cite: tāṃ me kathaya deveśa yena tṛptiṃ labhāmyaham | śṛṇu devi mahābhāge uttarasyāpyanuttaram

plain_english: This Kaula rite, O Goddess, standing in my heart-sky — I tell it, O lady of gods: it gives swift Kaula fruit.
sanskrit_cite: kauliko'yaṃ vidhirdevi mama hṛdvyomnyavasthitaḥ | kathayāmi sureśāni sadyaḥ kaulikasiddhidam

plain_english: First now: all lunar days, vowels ending in the drop; within them, by time's conjoining, moon and sun are named.
sanskrit_cite: athādyāstithayaḥ sarve svarā bindvavasānagāḥ | tadantaḥ kālayogena somasūryau prakīrtitau

plain_english: Realities from earth to person, in five groups in order — in ka-series, in sounds, ending with the ma-sound, O fair-vowed one.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthivyādīni tattvāni puruṣāntāni pañcasu | kramāt kādiṣu varṇeṣu makārānteṣu suvrate

plain_english: Fourfold the holds of wind, fire, water and their lords; above them, śa beginning the famed row, and before, the five Brahmas.
sanskrit_cite: vāyvāgnisalilendrāṇāṃ dhāraṇānāṃ catuṣṭayam | tadūrdhvaṃ śādi vikhyātaṃ purastādbrahmapañcakam

plain_english: Rootless, rightly ranged, to be known, ending in kṣa — this forthgoing declared; of all mantras indeed, and of wisdoms, O glorious one.
sanskrit_cite: amūlā tatkramājjñeyā kṣāntā sṛṣṭirudāhṛtā | sarveṣāmeva mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ ca yaśasvini

plain_english: This is the womb, told in all Tantras in every way — joined with the fourteen, O lucky one, joined with the tithi-lord's end; the third godhead, O fair-hipped, the heart of Bhairava himself.
sanskrit_cite: iyaṃ yoni samākhyātā sarvatantreṣu sarvathā | caturdaśayutaṃ bhadre tithīśāntasamanvitam tṛtīyaṃ brahma suśroṇi hṛdayaṃ bhairavātmanaḥ |
